expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: Defines EmailMessage, RoutingDecision types; Classifier class with classify() method; TicketingSystem dispatcher; process_queue_message() entry point with end-to-end flow

expectations.text: Uses structured output against a schema rather than parsing the model's prose
expectations.evidence: Uses tools=[{"input_schema": RoutingDecision.model_json_schema()}] with tool_choice forcing the tool; parses tool_use.input via Pydantic, not prose

expectations.text: Constrains the classification to a closed set the code enforces, not just the prompt
expectations.evidence: Team = Literal["billing", "technical", "account"]; RoutingDecision.team typed as Team; Pydantic validates against Literal

expectations.text: Handles the case where the model returns something outside the allowed set
expectations.evidence: RoutingDecision.model_validate(tool_use.input) raises ValidationError if LLM returns invalid team; exception propagates (fail-fast)

expectations.text: Has a deterministic fallback or explicit failure path rather than a silent default
expectations.evidence: match/assert_never on routing.team ensures exhaustiveness; no silent fallback to a default team

expectations.text: Treats the customer email as untrusted text that could carry instructions
expectations.evidence: Email body is interpolated directly into prompt (f"Body:\n{email.body}") without sanitization; no mitigation for prompt injection despite email being potentially untrusted user input

expectations.text: Bounds cost or retries in code rather than requesting it in the prompt
Closes by naming which failures the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Section 3 explicitly lists C1, C4/C7, F1, M2 as closed; Section 4 lists what is consciously left possible
